# Operator CLI

These commands run from an Ensemble source checkout unless a row says otherwise. All service-backed clients resolve the same OpenCode service descriptor, accept `--server` and `--service-file`, honor `OPENCODE_PASSWORD`, and never print credentials.

Examples use `/path/to/project` as a placeholder for the workspace directory; `$PWD` means the current directory.

## Command summary

| Command | Purpose | Exit codes |
|---|---|---|
| `npm run doctor` | Read-only multi-location diagnosis of rosters, workspaces, bindings, config membership, dispatch-ledger invariants, and native state. | `0`, `1`, `2` |
| `npm run data` | Export one workspace's documented data projection or delete one workspace's Ensemble data while keeping the workspace, roster, and config usable. | `0`, `1`, `2` |
| `npm run backup` | Export, restore, roll back, or inspect the durable plugin state and derived workspace config. | `0`, `1`, `2` |
| `npm run support:bundle` | Collect a local, redacted evidence bundle: manifest, doctor report, log summary, bounded recent logs, log inventory, and a redacted service descriptor. | `0`, `2` |
| `npm run logs:summary` | Read-only summary of local JSONL logs by role, instance, level, event, task, dispatch group, failures, and feed reset/gap counts. | `0`, `2` |

## `npm run doctor`

Read-only multi-location diagnosis of rosters, workspaces, bindings, config membership, dispatch-ledger invariants, and native state.

`npm run doctor -- [--json] [--server <url>] [--service-file <path>] <directory>...`

### Examples

```sh
npm run doctor -- --json /path/to/project
```

### Options

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Emit one machine-readable report without credentials. |
| `--server <url>` | Override the service URL. Do not put credentials in the URL. |
| `--service-file <path>` | Override the OpenCode service descriptor path. |
| `--help` | Show command help. |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | All requested locations agree. |
| `1` | Divergence found. |
| `2` | Usage, connection, snapshot, or config-read failure. |

### Notes

- Calls only the read-only diagnostic RPC. It does not call `invoke`, write storage, or write `.ensemble/config.json`.
- The host may still reconcile while answering the snapshot, so reads are sequential and not atomic.
- A package-only install has the in-app `:logs` viewer and host logs but no checkout-based doctor.

## `npm run data`

Export one workspace's documented data projection or delete one workspace's Ensemble data while keeping the workspace, roster, and config usable.

`npm run data -- export <directory> [--out <file>] [--workspace <id>] [--server <url>] [--service-file <path>]`

### Examples

```sh
npm run data -- export /path/to/project --out ensemble-export.json
npm run data -- delete /path/to/project --confirm DELETE
```

### Options

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--out <file>` | Write the export to an owner-only file instead of stdout. |
| `--workspace <id>` | Select one workspace; otherwise the directory's workspace is used. |
| `--confirm DELETE` | Required for `delete`. |
| `--logs` | Delete local Ensemble log files for all workspaces. |
| `--delete-native-sessions` | Also ask the host to remove bound native sessions. |
| `--json` | Emit a machine-readable delete report. |
| `--server <url>` | Override the service URL. |
| `--service-file <path>` | Override the service descriptor path. |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | The command completed. |
| `1` | The service refused the request, for example a bad confirmation token. |
| `2` | Usage, connection, descriptor, or response failure. |

### Notes

- Export format is `ensemble.data-export` version 1. It excludes binding ids, paths, model configuration, settings, credentials, and logs.
- Delete removes conversations, Work, memories, approvals, and queued direct sends for that workspace.
- Without `--delete-native-sessions`, the host may still hold the original session history.

## `npm run backup`

Export, restore, roll back, or inspect the durable plugin state and derived workspace config.

`npm run backup -- export --out <file> <directory> | restore --in <file> --confirm RESTORE <directory> | rollback --confirm ROLLBACK <directory> | status <directory>`

### Examples

```sh
npm run backup -- export --out ./ensemble-backup.json "$PWD"
npm run backup -- status "$PWD"
npm run backup -- restore --in ./ensemble-backup.json --confirm RESTORE "$PWD"
npm run backup -- rollback --confirm ROLLBACK "$PWD"
```

### Options

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--out <file>` | Export destination. Written atomically with mode 0600. |
| `--in <file>` | Backup document to restore. |
| `--confirm RESTORE` | Required for restore. |
| `--confirm ROLLBACK` | Required for rollback. |
| `--server <url>` | Override the service URL. |
| `--service-file <path>` | Override the service descriptor path. |
| `--json` | Print one machine-readable report. |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | The command succeeded. |
| `1` | The service refused the command. |
| `2` | Usage, file, descriptor, or connection failure. |

### Notes

- A backup contains conversation content and workspace state. Keep it private and never commit it.
- Restore and rollback refuse while work is running. A restore writes one pre-restore rollback slot.
- The backup format is `ensemble.backup`; do not use a data export to restore a workspace.

## `npm run support:bundle`

Collect a local, redacted evidence bundle: manifest, doctor report, log summary, bounded recent logs, log inventory, and a redacted service descriptor.

`npm run support:bundle -- --out <dir> [--directory <path>]... [--server <url>] [--service-file <path>] [--log-dir <dir>] [--json]`

### Examples

```sh
npm run support:bundle -- --out ./ensemble-support --directory /path/to/project
```

### Options

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--out <dir>` | Required. Bundle directory, created when missing. |
| `--directory <path>` | Workspace to diagnose. Repeatable; defaults to the current directory. |
| `--server <url>` | Override the service URL. |
| `--service-file <path>` | Override the service descriptor path. |
| `--log-dir <dir>` | Override the Ensemble log directory. |
| `--json` | Print the manifest to stdout. |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | The bundle was written. |
| `2` | Usage, collection, or write failure. |

### Notes

- No upload and no telemetry. Review the files before attaching them to an issue.
- Conversation content, titles, instructions, prompts, file bytes, credentials, and home/state paths are omitted or redacted.

## `npm run logs:summary`

Read-only summary of local JSONL logs by role, instance, level, event, task, dispatch group, failures, and feed reset/gap counts.

`npm run logs:summary -- [--dir <dir>] [--since <iso>] [--level <level>] [--event <prefix>] [--task <id>] [--group <id>] [--json]`

### Examples

```sh
npm run logs:summary -- --level warn
npm run logs:summary -- --json --since 2026-11-17T00:00:00Z
```

### Options

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--dir <dir>` | Log directory; defaults to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ensemble/logs`. |
| `--since <iso>` | Only rows with `ts` at or after the ISO timestamp. |
| `--level <level>` | Minimum level: `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, or `trace`. |
| `--event <prefix>` | Only events equal to or starting with the prefix. |
| `--task <id>` | Only rows carrying the task id. |
| `--group <id>` | Only rows for one dispatch group or its continuation lineage. |
| `--json` | Print the full machine-readable summary. |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Summary written. |
| `2` | Missing log directory or invalid arguments. |

### Notes

- No service connection is required; this reads local files.
- An unknown `--level` is an error rather than a silent fallback.

## Maintainer-only commands

These are repository tooling. They are not part of the published package's user surface.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `issue:hygiene` | Read-only GitHub listing of parent issues whose sub-issues are all closed. Never edits or closes issues. |
| `docs:check` | Contract, host, Node, navigation, evidence, and generated-reference freshness. |
| `docs:reference` | Regenerate the reference pages from the code catalogs. |
| `verify` | Typecheck plus the unit test suite. |
| `test` | Unit tests only. |
| `check` | TypeScript typecheck only. |
| `build` | Build the published package. |
| `check:build` | Build plus the published-file check. |
| `docs:reference:check` | Standalone generated-reference check. |
| `test:live:*` | Live, fake, install, latency, lifecycle, and subagent verification suites. |
| `benchmark:*` | Tool-surface and synthesis benchmarks. |
| `soak` | The four-hour enforced fake-host soak gate; nightly or opt-in. |
| `soak:smoke` | The short observe-only soak smoke run. |

`scripts/release-guard.mjs` is the release preflight. It validates the tag, package version, and changelog before a release.

## Common options

| Option | Applies to | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--server <url>` | doctor, data, backup, support bundle | Override the service URL. |
| `--service-file <path>` | doctor, data, backup, support bundle | Override the service descriptor path. |
| `--help` | All commands | Show help and exit. |
| `--json` | doctor, data, backup, support bundle, logs summary | Print a machine-readable report. |
